concepts.note: The income-side estimate of nominal GDP. The GDP-GDI gap is itself a measurement-error signal, so both are worth carrying.

Kept separate from nominal GDI rather than listed as a substitute for it. A deflated series and its nominal twin are different quantities, and the redundancy detector flagged the original single-concept version of this entry on its first run.
All levels of government (federal + state + local) — the G in GDP's C+I+G+NX. Distinct from the fiscal family's federal-only FGCE, which measures federal budget policy specifically.
GDP less inventory change — demand without the restocking cycle.
SIC-basis (IPMANSICS) runs back to 1919; NAICS-basis (IPMAN) is the current classification standard but only starts 1972. Same concept, two classification eras.
Retail inventory/sales. The channel a demand miss shows up in first.
Cass/BTS freight shipments. A physical-volume cross-check on the survey-based activity measures.
Weekly and noisy, and its secular decline is a modal-shift story rather than a cycle. Registry context, not a factor input.
A third of core CPI on its own, and the slowest-moving third.
Imputed, not transacted, and it lags market rents by roughly a year — which is why it has to be separable from the rest.
The number the FOMC statement refers to.
Quarterly only — no monthly cut of this component exists on FRED.
Excludes imputed prices. If it diverges from core PCE the difference is measurement convention, not inflation.

concepts.concept: PPI final demand ex food and energy
concepts.note: BLS retired the 'finished goods' PPI methodology for 'final demand' in 2014; WPSFD4131 is the older finished-goods cut with deeper history, PPIFES the current final-demand one.
PPIITM stopped updating in 2015 (BLS moved to the WPUID6x family); WPUID61 is the current series and listed first.
The tariff and dollar channel into goods inflation.
Compensation per unit of output — the wage channel net of productivity, which average hourly earnings alone cannot give.
Already an annualised rate, so differenced rather than double-log-differenced.
Restricted to slow-repricing components, so it is closer to the persistent part than core is.
Holds job mix fixed, so it does not move when the composition of employment shifts. Quarterly.
University of Michigan household expectations. A survey, kept in the soft layer so it never silently substitutes for a price.
The first margin employers cut, so it leads the headline.
Free of the participation denominator, so it cannot improve because people stopped looking.
The other employment survey. A persistent payrolls/household gap is a measurement signal in its own right.
Thin and noisy monthly; registry context.
The highest-frequency labour read there is, five days behind.
Ex autos, gas and building materials — the slice that maps into the GDP consumption estimate.
The big-ticket, credit-financed end, where a rate shock lands first.
Earned income only — the cut the NBER dating committee watches.
Debt payments as a share of disposable income — the affordability constraint that credit outstanding alone does not show.
OECD's US confidence indicator. The Conference Board series itself is not redistributable through FRED.
FRED holds a 13-month rolling window under NAR licensing, so there is no history to fetch. Recorded so the absence is attributable to the licence rather than to an oversight.
Purchase-only and repeat-sales, quarterly. A second price measurement with different coverage from Case-Shiller.
NAR composite; discontinued/licence-limited on FRED. Carried as a concept so the gap is visible.
Non-defence ex aircraft — the same signal with the two worst sources of noise removed.
Already a standardised composite centred on zero, so level. Built from 85 indicators, which makes it a useful external check on whatever the global factor turns out to be.
Dallas Fed calls its headline series general business activity, not manufacturing, unlike the other regional surveys here.
Confirmed absent: FRED search returns no Kansas City Fed manufacturing series under any query tried. The Fed publishes it directly; not mirrored through FRED's API.
Confirmed absent from FRED under any query tried; same gap as the Kansas City survey.
The New York Fed's series has moved on and off FRED. Probed rather than assumed.
ISM withdrew redistribution rights, so the FRED series ends in 2020 or 404s. Kept as a concept because its ABSENCE is the reason the regional surveys are carried.
FRED's ICE BofA licence exposes a rolling window only — roughly three years, so it cannot anchor a long backtest.
Moody's, daily back to 1986 — the long credit-stress history the ICE series lacks.
Baa minus Aaa is the part of the spread that is default risk rather than duration.
Same concept nine days behind instead of six weeks. Both are carried: one has the history, the other has the edge.
The only direct read on credit SUPPLY. Quantities cannot distinguish nobody wanting to borrow from nobody being allowed to.

No broad residential-mortgage tightening series on FRED; only narrow post-2015 cuts by loan type (DRTSSP for subprime, and GSE-eligible/QM/non-QM equivalents), none of which covers what this concept means. DRTSCILM (C&I tightening) carries the credit-supply signal for this panel instead.
Not on FRED under any query tried; the series would in any case be quarterly and statutorily distorted by the 2005 reform.
Starts 2018. The post-LIBOR funding benchmark.
IOER stopped 2021-07-28, IORB started 2021-07-29 — a direct handoff when the Fed eliminated the required/excess reserve distinction, not two measurements of different things.
The slope with the better recession record, because its front end is the policy rate rather than an expectation of it.
105 indicators on one zero-centred scale. Its vintage archive begins 2011-05 whatever start is requested.
NFCI with the part explained by the real economy projected out.
A CONSTRUCTED index, not a quote: the H.10 basket weights are re-estimated annually and applied backwards, so it disagrees with its own archive on 91% of days. It needs the vintage route.
FRED serves a rolling ten-year window, so this cannot carry a long backtest.
Confirmed absent from FRED under any query tried; may have been discontinued. S&P 500 is the equity level actually in the panel.
The 2020 definitional change makes the level incomparable across that break; the second log difference survives it.
The quantity balance-sheet policy operates on directly, weekly.
Moves reserves around without any policy decision, which is why it belongs beside WALCL rather than inside a reading of it.
The drain that stood between the balance sheet and reserves through 2022-2024.
Quarterly and thin; interpretation context.
'Current receipts' (all receipts: taxes, fees, transfers from business). W006RC1Q027SBEA (tax receipts only) is narrower scope, not offered as a substitute.
'Current expenditures'. W019RCQ027SBEA ('total' expenditures) may include capital outlays FGEXPND excludes; not offered as a substitute without confirming the scope.
A level in dollars that crosses zero, so it cannot be logged.
Federal only. GCE (all levels of government) is a different, broader quantity — carried separately under output_activity, since it is literally the G in GDP's C+I+G+NX.

concepts.concept: federal debt held by the public
concepts.note: Excludes intragovernmental holdings (e.g. the Social Security trust fund). GFDEBTN (gross federal debt) is a different, larger quantity — carried as its own concept.
Includes intragovernmental holdings; the debt-ceiling quantity, distinct from debt held by the public.
Crosses zero by construction, so level.
A stock, not a flow, and quarterly. Registry context for the external sector rather than a factor input.
The classic industrial-demand proxy; monthly on FRED.

The LBMA daily fixing FRED used to carry is gone; FRED search returns nothing under 'gold price'. IQ12260 (Export Price Index: Nonmonetary Gold) exists but is a trade-price concept, not a spot quote, so it is not offered as a substitute here.
New York Fed index. Not served by FRED; recorded so the gap is attributable to the source rather than to the audit.
EIA weekly/monthly production series are not mirrored on FRED; they require EIA's own API and a separate key. Out of scope for this pass — recorded as a known gap, not silently dropped.
Same EIA-API gap as crude production.
Same EIA-API gap as crude production.
Same EIA-API gap as crude production.

The utilization rate itself is EIA-API only. IPG32411S (Industrial Production: petroleum refining) is a volume proxy on FRED and is carried as its own concept below instead of being offered as a substitute for a rate.
A volume proxy for refinery activity, since the EIA utilization RATE is not on FRED.
Same EIA-API gap as crude production.
Same EIA-API gap as crude production.
IP: utilities is the FRED-native proxy for electricity output.

concepts.concept: nondefense capital goods orders ex aircraft

concepts.note: AMNMNO (originally listed as an alternate) turned out to be nondurable-goods new ORDERS — a different concept entirely, not a substitute. ANDEVS is total nondefense capital goods shipments; no ex-aircraft cut of shipments (as opposed to orders, where NEWORDER already provides one) was found on FRED.
Private only, matching 'business' investment. TLNRESCONS (total, public+private) is a different, broader quantity.
A ratio, so differenced. The margin measure that does not need constructing from two series.

UMCSENT1 is not a current-conditions component — it is the PREDECESSOR of UMCSENT itself, discontinued in 1977 when UMCSENT began. The current-conditions sub-index is not separately published on FRED; UMCSENT (the composite, already a concept above) is what is actually available.
NFIB is not redistributed through FRED. Recorded as a known hole.
Not an expectation — it carries a risk premium — but it is the daily one, against surveys that are monthly at best.
Strips the near-term energy pass-through out of breakevens.
